knowledge_point.title: Differentiating a Sum of Functions Without Constant Factors Using the Sum Rule

question.:question/worked-solution:
The function $f(x)$ is the sum of three power functions. So, we apply the sum rule, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2}+\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}-x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{-2})-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x) \\  & =2{x}^{(2-1)}+(-2){x}^{(-2-1)}-1 \\  & =2{x}^{1}-2{x}^{-3}-1 \\  & =2{x}^{1}-\frac{2}{{x}^{3}}-1.\end{aligned}
$$

generation.sampling_policy: Explicit bounded exponent extension; radio a=2..6,b=2..4; blank a=3..7, fixed 4/3 root term; source coefficient magnitudes remain one

question.:question/worked-solution:
The function $f(x)$  is the sum of two power functions. So, we apply the sum rule, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{3}+\sqrt[3]{{x}^{4}}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{3})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{4/3}) \\  & =3{x}^{(3-1)}+\frac{4}{3}{x}^{(4/3-1)} \\  & =3{x}^{2}+\frac{4}{3}{x}^{1/3} \\  & =3{x}^{2}+\frac{4}{3}\sqrt[3]{x}.\end{aligned}
$$
